findings.problem: At the end of [3:13] the reader knows only her name. The snapshot already states her private income [3:17], her stepfather [3:20-21] and that her fiancé vanished on the wedding morning, which is only told at [3:56]. The story's premise is also in the cast-list thread, so this is not a plot spoiler, but the snapshot runs ahead of the text. Typist and short sight (her ordinary identity) are fine.
findings.evidence: [3:13] "the boy in buttons entered to announce Miss Mary Sutherland"; the disappearance is first told at [3:56] "when the cabman got down from the box and looked there was no one there!"
findings.fix: Move this snapshot's gate from [3:13] to [3:17] and change BODY to: "A short-sighted young typist with a small private income of her own. She has come to Holmes in distress to find out what has become of her fiancé, Mr. Hosmer Angel."

findings.problem: At [3:17] the only thing known is that Mary wants to know 'what has become of' him. The first card adds the ball, the engagement, the cab vanishing ([3:30]-[3:56]) and the tinted glasses and soft voice ([3:50]). Those two details are the very disguise clues Holmes later relies on. The card also gives Mary's view of him ('gentleman') as plain fact, without saying it is hers.
findings.evidence: [3:17] "I would give it all to know what has become of Mr. Hosmer Angel."; [3:50] "a hesitating, whispering fashion of speech ... he wore tinted glasses against the glare"
findings.fix: BODY from [3:17]: "The man Mary Sutherland was engaged to. He has disappeared, and she has come to Holmes to find out what became of him." Add a snapshot gated at [3:56] with BODY: "A shy, softly spoken gentleman, as Mary describes him, whom she met at the gasfitters’ ball and became engaged to. On their wedding morning he got into a separate cab to the church and was not in it when it arrived."

findings.problem: The last sentence, about vanishing at the church door to keep her bound, comes from Holmes's account at [3:126], two paragraphs after the gate. Paragraph [3:124] ends with him appearing as Hosmer Angel.
findings.evidence: [3:126] "James Windibank wished Miss Sutherland to be so bound to Hosmer Angel ... As far as the church door he brought her, and then ... he conveniently vanished away"
findings.fix: Cut the final sentence "He then vanished at the church door to leave her bound to a missing fiancé." from the [3:124] snapshot. Either add a snapshot at [3:126] that restores it, or leave it out, since the [3:129] snapshot already covers the outcome.

findings.problem: 'leaving behind only a newspaper description' suggests Angel left the description behind. In fact Mary placed the advertisement herself after he vanished.
findings.evidence: [3:72] "I advertised for him in last Saturday’s Chronicle," said she. "Here is the slip and here are four letters from him."
findings.fix: "The shy, soft-voiced gentleman Mary met at the gasfitters’ ball and quickly became engaged to. He disappeared from his cab between home and church; all she has of him is the description she advertised and four typewritten letters."

findings.problem: Her card never changes after [3:13], so readers at the end of the story see nothing about how her case ends for her. Holmes decides not to tell her the truth, and this matters for her character.
findings.evidence: [3:136] "If I tell her she will not believe me."
findings.fix: Add a snapshot gated at [3:136]: "A short-sighted young typist with a small private income. Her vanished fiancé ‘Hosmer Angel’ was her stepfather in disguise, but Holmes decides not to tell her, believing she would not accept it. She has vowed to stay true to Hosmer."

findings.problem: The text never says Mrs. Etherege was Holmes's client. It says only that Holmes found her husband and that she told Mary about him.
findings.evidence: [3:17] "I heard of you from Mrs. Etherege, whose husband you found so easy when the police and everyone had given him up for dead."
